﻿# 两个开源项目，让他年入6位数

## 冷启动：从小痴迷计算机

Manuel 背景是 computer science。

Fascinated by computers since child，growing up in eighties。

Started programming at early age。

Quite natural studied computer science for graduate studies。

Currently spends most time on two projects：

**BullMQ**：Open-source distributed job processing library built on top of Redis。

**Castmill**：Open-source digital signage solution。

Currently in six-figure ARR range。

Growing at around 50% yearly。

## 反直觉：他开始只是想解决自己的问题

Wrote BullMQ as side project to be used in Castmill。

Needed reliable queue service for NodeJS。

Weren't any happy with at time — this was 2011-2012。

So wrote library based on Redis to fulfill needs。

Published library as open source on NPM。

Later，started getting issue reports on GitHub。

Surprised so many people finding library useful。

Just happy able to contribute to open source community with useful piece of software。

But as years passed，number of issues started to grow。

Not only bug fixes，but new feature requests。

Which happily implement if not too big。

Came to point where started to think about viability of project。

Could only work on it in spare time。

But since so popular，thought might be opportunity for monetization。

## 暴击：6个月的努力全白费了

Thought maybe could add something extra to attract more customers。

Since BullMQ based on Redis。

Figured offering Redis hosting solution built into dashboard would be huge success。

Had many thousands of users using open-source library。

Were in need of hosting solution。

What could be better than buying from creator of BullMQ itself？

Spent about six months building this feature。

Then released it。

Turned out to be disaster。

Not only growth super slow — even slower than dashboard subscription itself。

But also kept losing sleep。

Hosting issues and customers would get angry because Redis offline。

Had to throw that solution away。

Realized going to burn him out。

Instead，pivoted to professional version of library。

Turned out to be most successful pivot。

In hindsight，should have understood unfair advantage was knowledge in queue technology。

Whereas hosting was something new。

##  punchline：Indie hacker 需要 stubborn

If considering starting business as indie hacker。

Remember not to lose hope。

Even though sometimes feels like way to success very long。

For some lucky people，success overnight story。

But for most，will require lot of work and sacrifice。

Be prepared for that。

Being stubborn，in positive way，going to be one of most valuable traits。

Also，reserve some time to reflect on past and keep reprioritizing task list。

Things feel super important today may not be that important in couple of days。
